questions.q: What does the standard User object represent, per this lesson?
options: A field on the Account object, not a standalone object
A real Salesforce record for anyone who logs into the org, with fields like Name, Email, Profile, and Role
A feature only available in Salesforce Platform licenses
An invisible system layer that isn't stored as an actual record
questions.explain: Users are real records on the standard User object, like any other object, including a Name and Email.

questions.q: Per this lesson, what determines the hard ceiling on what a user could possibly be granted access to, before profiles even come into play?
options: The number of records they've personally created
The user's license
The order the user was created in relative to other users
The user's chosen display language
questions.explain: The lesson describes a license as the hard boundary that exists before profiles or permission sets are even considered.

questions.q: What does a Salesforce Platform license grant, compared to a full Salesforce license?
options: Unlimited access to every object plus admin rights
Full access to Accounts, Contacts, and Opportunities, identical to a full Salesforce license
Only the ability to log in, with zero object access of any kind
Access to custom objects/apps built on the platform, but not standard CRM Sales/Service Cloud functionality
questions.explain: The Platform license is a lower-cost license for custom-app users, explicitly without standard CRM object access.

questions.q: Per this lesson, what license type is described as mostly for collaboration (Chatter posts, groups) without real object-level CRM access?
options: Chatter Free / Chatter External
Salesforce license
Sales Cloud Enterprise license
Salesforce Platform license
questions.explain: Chatter Free/External licenses are limited to collaboration features, not CRM object access.

questions.q: Why does this lesson say a colleague's license is worth checking if they claim they 'can't find' an object you know exists?
options: Missing objects are always a data-entry error, never a license issue
A Platform-licensed user genuinely cannot see standard CRM objects the way a full Salesforce-licensed user can, regardless of their profile
Only admins are ever affected by license restrictions
License type has no effect on which objects a user can see
questions.explain: The lesson explicitly names license mismatches as a real, common cause of a user not seeing an object they'd expect to.
